channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Don't Get Used To It"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This really hit me somewhere where stories I normally read don't. Probably has something to do with the fact that I have friends that went through abuse as a kid to the point where it's almost acceptable to them and having to say that it isn't still surprises them and throws them back to reality even today. Really puts the fact that the scariest things in life aren't monsters or demons, but they're the thoughts of our own species and the fucked up actions that people do every day behind the mask of secrecy and public image.

+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
mundane horror

So this is exactly what I wanted to write this tale around. I remember hearing someone off-handedly mention that their parents would hit them, like it’s a totally normal thing that’s supposed to happen. I’ve luckily never had to deal with that, but the sheer thought threw me for a loop. The concept felt so foreign to me, and it was incredibly evocative. So much so that I wrote this tale about it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I've written a lot of fucked up things.

I've written about children having their eyes eaten. Unicorns which are zebras with machetes on their heads. Lotus eater machines. Endless cycles of death.

Nothing I ever write will ever come close to human evil, in its intensity or insidiousness.

+1, for reminding me that the truest horror is the mundane horror we all put each other through.
